title: Took your feedback, new pricing  a portfolio builder, and a lot of engine changes
author: Xqvlzz
selftext:
Posted here a while back and got some honest feedback. A lot of it was fair, so here’s what I changed.

**Pricing.** Free accounts get 3 backtests when you verify your email. Paid plans are £15, £40 and £85 a month for 25, 50 and 150 tests. Simpler than the old token maths.

**Portfolio building.** Describe a portfolio in plain English, like “10 large US companies outside tech that pay a dividend, lowest volatility”. It shows the conditions it read, then picks the companies by code, not AI. It only uses prices, share counts and dividends from before the test starts, and it tells you the company list itself is today’s. You can edit the list, then test it. Or just name your own companies and it runs them straight away.

**Ask about a portfolio.** On any portfolio or shared result you can ask things like “what drove the returns” or “how risky was this”. The basic ones (did it beat the S&P over the same dates, the risk in plain words) are free, and the answers only use that portfolio’s own figures.

# Engine changes, mostly from your guys  comments:

* Every test now runs a luck check: the same rule on random entry days and on shuffled prices. A result only says it beat buy and hold if it clears that.
* The most recent months stay sealed on your first long test of an idea (12 months on a 5 year test). You tune on the earlier years, then open the sealed months once.
* Prove it now includes a fold-by-fold walk-forward.
* Monte Carlo runs 10,000 paths, with block sizes chosen from your own returns, plus a panel showing how the rule did through the S&P’s big falls.
* The deflated Sharpe counts every version of the idea you’ve tested, not just the one in front of you.
* It shows you what it read from your prompt before it runs, and it reads company names, so Tesla works, not just TSLA.

We also built a deliberate overfit: 840 rules, picked the best looking three, and published what the checks did to them. They got caught.

No return screenshots on purpose. The point is you can see exactly how a result was made and whether to trust it.

Still interested in some more feedback tell me what breaks! [quantistrade.co.uk](http://quantistrade.co.uk)

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body: telling people the company list is today's is more honesty than most tools manage. a dividend screen run back five years on today's names quietly skips every company that cut its payout or went under along the way.
